title: Fridgeberg's Challenge
statementMd:
Fridgeberg is a well-known veteran in the Taiwanese ICPC community. He specializes in counting problems. Since he solves counting problems faster than everyone else, people call him a speed-counter. Today, he has prepared a challenge for you along with the following message.

"Yo, I'm Fridgeberg, and I'm an 18-year-old ICPC speed-counter from Yunlin, Taiwan. Today, I'm challenging you to a counting problem."

The challenge is as follows.

A rooted labelled tree with n𝑛 vertices is a tree with vertices labelled 1,2,…,n1,2,…,𝑛 and one vertex chosen as the root.

Recall that for any two vertices in a tree, there is a unique simple path connecting them. For each vertex v𝑣 in a rooted labelled tree, define its subtree as the set of all vertices u𝑢 such that v𝑣 is on the unique path from the root to u𝑢. In particular, a vertex is always in its own subtree. The subtrees of a tree are the collection of all vertices' subtrees.

A rooted labelled tree is k𝑘-free if none of its subtrees has exactly k𝑘 vertices.

For each k𝑘 from 22 to n−1𝑛−1, compute the number of different rooted labelled trees with n𝑛 vertices that are k𝑘-free. Since the numbers can be very large, please compute them modulo 998244353998244353.

Two rooted labelled trees are different if at least one of the following holds:

- The labels of the roots are different.
- There exists an edge that is present in one tree but not in the other.

## Input

The only line contains a single integer n𝑛.

- 3≤n≤2×1053≤𝑛≤2×105

## Output

Output n−2𝑛−2 lines. On the i𝑖-th line, output the answer when k=i+1𝑘=𝑖+1.

## Note

**Explanation for Sample 1**

There are exactly 33 rooted labelled trees that have no subtree with exactly 22 vertices.
